description: I'm interested in projects involving Earth and space data. I want to create and develop interactive applications and tools that will make complicated information easier for people to understand.
summary: This health companion prototype helps a crew organize their health and wellbeing during space missions. Users can record and review their heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose and temperature, as well as their activity and moods. Our idea for this challenge should provide history of health, hazard info, and emergency training scenarios into one interface. The system includes essential resources and will store data locally for offline use. With this, we hope the crew can provide an easier way to record, review, and handoff to medical professionals.
details:
Deep Space Health Systems is a prototype designed to assist astronauts track their health during missions where there is limited access to medical professionals.


Our users will experience daily check-ins. They can record blood pressure, blood glucose, heart rate, and body temperature and review each reading before storing it locally to their device. The health check option will provide indicators, symptoms, guidance, and follow-up steps in one place. A field guide can explain how the crew member may take measurements and why they are important.

Our team believes that health is more than just vital signs. The Wellbeing option gives our crew a way to record mood, sleep, meals, and exercise. We also added emergency training scenarios and a game called Move the Moon for a bit of fun.

We built this application with limited connection in mind. It is designed so that the tools and records are available on the device without internet access. Users can export a report to share when it is appropriate. This prototype includes a connection for compatible Bluetooth sensors depending on the device used.

This project was built using Next.JS, TypeScript, and TailwindCSS. NASA's human research resources helped our understanding of hazards astronauts may face including radiation, isolation, and altered gravity. Our goal is to make it easier to record, review and discuss health information.
